The `.codex` symlink also prevents **every shell command in this session** from starting:

> cannot enforce sandbox read-only path …/.codex because it crosses writable symlink

I couldn’t inspect configuration or change files.

To unblock this, run locally from the repository root:

```sh
for dir in .codex .claude; do
  if [ -L "$dir" ]; then
    cp -aL "$dir" "$dir.real" &&
      unlink "$dir" &&
      mv "$dir.real" "$dir"
  fi
done
entire doctor
```

This preserves the existing contents while replacing the symlinks with real directories. Then restart this Codex session so I can reconcile the shared configuration, Git tracking, and Entire hooks.
I’ll check whether the directories are now accessible, then continue fixing the Entire configuration.
